setup_summary.text: Home Depot reports fiscal Q3 2026 on 2026-11-17 (time not confirmed). Finnhub labels it 'fiscal Q3 2027', but the filings call the same period fiscal Q3 2026. Consensus is EPS $3.95 and revenue $44.04B. Against the year-ago GAAP EPS of $3.62 and revenue of $41.35B, that implies +9.2% EPS and +6.5% revenue growth.
Q2 FY26 (ended Aug 2): net sales were $47.86B (+5.7%) and diluted EPS was $4.79 (+4.6%). Operating margin was 14.3% against 14.5% a year earlier.

Q2 quality of earnings: Home Depot received about $730M of IEEPA tariff refunds, 'the vast majority' of what it expects. About $685M reduced cost of goods sold and the rest reduced inventory cost, nearly all in the Primary segment. My arithmetic: $685M is about 143bp of Q2 sales, or about $0.52 per share after tax at the 24.5% rate and about 996M diluted shares. Q2 GAAP EPS excluding the refund is therefore about $4.27 against $4.58 a year ago, about -7%. This is my calculation, not a company figure.

Core (Primary) segment excluding the refund looks weaker than the headline. Primary sales grew only about 1.5% ($42,806M vs $42,157M) while Primary SG&A grew about 5.3% ($7,766M vs $7,375M). Primary operating income was $6,592M vs $6,354M. Removing the $685M refund (nearly all in Primary) gives a Primary operating margin of about 13.8% against 15.1% a year earlier, roughly -130bp. This is my calculation.

Demand: Q2 comparable sales were +1.7%, with comparable transactions -1.0% and comparable average ticket +2.8%. FX added about 25bp to comps. Management cited customer engagement with smaller repair and maintenance projects despite consumer uncertainty and housing affordability pressure. H1 comps were +1.2%, with transactions -1.2%.
H1 operating income grew only 1.1% on sales growth of 5.3%. H1 operating margin was 13.2% against 13.7%, and H1 EPS growth was +0.7%.

Acquired distribution drives reported growth. Other (SRS/GMS/HVAC) sales were $5,055M against $3,120M. GMS contributed $1.4B of sales in Q2 (it was acquired Sept 4, 2025). Mingledorff's (about $1.1B, closed May 11) was 'immaterial' to sales. Other operating income was $247M against $201M, a margin of about 4.9% against 6.4%. Roofing fell to about 39% of Other sales from about 62%.

Capital allocation: buybacks have been paused since March 2024 and Home Depot has no plan to resume them in fiscal 2026 as it seeks to cut debt. H1 included $3.0B of long-term debt repayment. TTM ROIC fell to 24.8% from 27.2%, driven by higher average equity from the buyback pause. H1 operating cash flow was $11.42B (+27.4%), helped by working-capital timing and lower tax payments.

Leadership: the 10-Q is signed by CFO Richard McPhail as 'Interim Principal Executive Officer', whereas the March 10-K was signed by Ted Decker as Chair, President and CEO. A NAW listing carries the headline 'Home Depot CEO Decker Takes Medical Leave; Interim Leaders Named', dated Aug 12, 2026. I found no successor-search news and no update since August.

Positioning: the options market implies a move of about ±7.2% (as of Oct 30) against an average closing move of about ±2.1% over the last 8 reports. The stock was down 17.3% over 52 weeks as of Oct 28.

last_reported.text: Q2 FY26 net sales were $47.86B (+5.7%), including GMS at $1.4B.

consensus.text: Consensus is $44.04B, +6.5% against $41.35B a year earlier.

view.text: My bottom-up view is about $42.7B to $43.2B (+3.3% to +4.5%), which puts $44.04B about 2% to 3% too high. GMS was owned for only about 8 weeks of Q3 FY25 (it generated $2.0B in about 21 weeks to Feb 1), so the GMS year-over-year increment shrinks to roughly $0.3B to $0.6B from $1.4B in Q2. Mingledorff's adds an estimated $0.2B to $0.3B (undisclosed). Primary segment growth was only about 1.5% in Q2. Consensus therefore needs organic growth of roughly double Q2's. These are my estimates.

metrics_to_model.metric: Diluted EPS (GAAP) and the adjusted-basis question

last_reported.text: Q2 FY26 GAAP diluted EPS was $4.79 (+4.6%) against $4.58. Q3 FY25 GAAP EPS was $3.62.

consensus.text: Consensus is $3.95, +9.2% against GAAP $3.62. The basis (GAAP or adjusted) is unconfirmed. Press cites FY25 EPS of $14.69 as the base, which is the adjusted figure, not GAAP $14.23, so the consensus probably is adjusted.

view.text: Adjusted EPS appears to equal GAAP plus after-tax acquired-intangible amortization. Q2 amortization of $178M adds about $0.13 per share, and FY25 amortization of $607M adds about $0.46, which bridges $14.23 to $14.69. On that basis Q3 FY25 adjusted EPS is about $3.75 (my derivation, with an assumed even Q3/Q4 amortization split), so $3.95 is only about +5%, not +9%. On my $43.0B revenue view and a 12.8% to 13.1% GAAP operating margin, GAAP EPS comes out about $3.74 to $3.84 (24.5% tax, about $565M interest and other, about 997M shares). The risk is skewed to a miss if $3.95 is a GAAP figure and roughly in line if it is adjusted. The Nov 17 release should state which basis is used.

last_reported.text: Q2 comps were +1.7% (transactions -1.0%, ticket +2.8%). H1 comps were +1.2%.

view.text: I lean to a Q3 comp of about 0% to +1.5%, ticket-led, with transactions still negative. Lowe's Q2 comps were only +0.2% (transactions -2.1%, ticket +2.3%) and it described persistent DIY pressure, with growth from Pro and online. University of Michigan sentiment was 48.0 in October, the second-lowest reading in the survey's 74-year history. New-home sales were 676k in September, down 5.3% year on year. Framing lumber was down 4.6% year on year, which is a small drag on ticket. The upside risk is Pro strength and share gains. The unreported part is Home Depot's own quarter-to-date commentary, which I could not cite. The guided full-year comp of flat to +2%, with H1 at +1.2%, implies an H2 comp of roughly -1% to +3%.

last_reported.text: Q2 gross margin was 33.7% against 33.4%. The refund added about 143bp by my arithmetic. Fuel, energy and input costs and the GMS mix largely offset it. H1 gross margin was 33.4% against 33.6%.

view.text: I expect a year-over-year decline in Q3 gross margin. The $685M recognised refund does not recur, and management expects fuel, energy and input costs to fully offset the refunds over the year. About $45M of refund sat in inventory and releases as that inventory sells, worth about $0.03 per share, mostly in Q3 on my inventory-turn inference. Mix drag from GMS and Mingledorff's persists. A TIKR summary of the Aug call says refund timing could shift some margin between Q2 and Q3. FY25 H2 gross margin was about 33.0%, which is my derivation. Lowe's gross margin fell 77bp in its Q2 even with refunds and acquisition mix.

last_reported.text: Q2 operating margin was 14.3% against 14.5%. H1 was 13.2% against 13.7%.

consensus.text: Not published. By my arithmetic, $3.95 EPS on $44.04B needs about a 13.1% GAAP operating margin, assuming about 997M shares (997.7M outstanding at Aug 18), a 24.5% tax rate (Q2 rate) and about $565M of interest and other, net (my assumption; Q2 was $524M including refund interest). That gives about $5.8B of operating income. Whether $3.95 is a GAAP or an adjusted figure is not stated in the sources.

view.text: I estimate Q3 FY25 operating margin at about 12.8%, derived from EPS because the Q3 FY25 operating income is not in the sources. The FY26 operating margin guide of 12.4% to 12.6% implies an H2 margin of roughly 11.5% to 11.9% against about 11.6% in H2 FY25, so management is guiding roughly flat to +30bp for H2. Q3 is seasonally richer than the H2 average. My view is a Q3 GAAP margin of about 12.5% to 13.1%, so a GAAP-basis $3.95 looks stretched.

last_reported.text: Q2 SG&A rose 8.5% to $8.4B (17.6% of sales against 17.1%), on sales growth of 5.7%. Primary SG&A rose about 5.3% on Primary sales growth of about 1.5%. Management attributes it to higher operating costs relative to comp performance.

view.text: Expect continued SG&A deleverage in the core. Comps near +1% do not cover wage and other cost growth. The GMS lap does not help SG&A as much as sales. Amortization, a separate D&A line, runs about $180M per quarter (remaining FY26 estimate $359M). Management has not quantified wage, fuel or integration costs.

metrics_to_model.metric: Other segment (SRS, GMS, HVAC) sales and operating margin

last_reported.text: Q2 Other sales were $5,055M (+62%) and operating income was $247M, a margin of about 4.9% against 6.4%. H1 Other sales were $9,057M.

view.text: Other should step down in growth after the Sept 4 GMS anniversary. I model about $4.4B to $4.7B of Other sales, and Primary near $38.3B (my estimates). Legacy SRS organic growth cannot be isolated: Mingledorff's revenue is undisclosed and roofing is now only about 39% of Other sales. With about $360M of FY26 remaining amortization and mix, Other margin likely stays below last year's 6.4%.

last_reported.text: Q2 interest and other, net was $524M (interest expense $583M, offset by $59M of interest income that includes interest on the tariff refunds). The effective tax rate was 24.5% (H1 24.7%). Diluted shares were 996M.

view.text: My assumption is interest and other, net of about $560M to $570M (Q2 was $524M and included interest received on IEEPA tariff refunds; the year-ago quarter was $550M), a tax rate near 24.5% to 25% (Q2 was 24.5%) and about 996M to 998M shares (Q2 diluted 996M; 997.7M outstanding at Aug 18), since buybacks are paused. Management does not plan to resume repurchases in fiscal 2026 as it seeks to reduce debt, so there is no buyback offset to EPS in FY26. Commercial paper was $4.2B at Aug 2. The $1.3B and $1.5B senior notes were already repaid in April and June, and the 10-K shows $1.0B (2.125%) and $750M (4.95%) senior notes due September 2026.

view.text: H1 cash flow was flattered by working-capital and tax timing, so I would not extrapolate +27%. Dividends run at about $2.3B per quarter. Deleveraging pace sets when buybacks resume, and no buyback is planned in FY26.

since_filing.text: No guidance change found since the Aug 18 reaffirmation. A Trefis article dated Oct 28 still describes the August guide as unchanged from May: sales +2.5% to +4.5%, comps flat to +2%, operating margin 12.4% to 12.6%.
Street FY26 EPS is $15.01, up 2.2% from $14.69 (the adjusted FY25 figure), per a Oct 28 preview. That supports reading the consensus as adjusted. The stock was down 17.3% over 52 weeks at that date.

Consumer backdrop worsened. University of Michigan sentiment was 48.0 in October, the second-lowest reading in the survey's 74-year history, with inflation squeezing budgets and a fuel supply shortage keeping gasoline prices high.

Housing remains weak. New-home sales were 676k annualized in September, -5.3% year on year and 2.9% below 2025 year to date, with builders cutting prices and buyers reluctant amid elevated mortgage rates. Framing lumber was $499.01 per 1,000 board feet on Oct 16, down 3.3% month on month and 4.6% year on year.

Supplier read-through is mixed. Masco reported Q3 net sales of $1.96B (+3%), a 17.9% operating margin and a raised 2026 EPS outlook to $4.65 to $4.75. It cited mid-single-digit input cost inflation and an estimated net tariff-refund benefit of about $85M for the year.
A TIKR summary (Oct 24) of the Aug call says management flagged that the timing of tariff refunds could shift some margin between Q2 and Q3, and notes Q2 gross margin rose about 25bp to 33.7%.

Trefis (Oct 22) says SRS is growing faster than Home Depot as a whole, but that Home Depot's operating margin has slipped for three years and its Q2 gross margin rose only because of the refund. It names operating margin versus the 12.4% to 12.6% guide as the number to watch.

Lowe's, the main peer, last reported Q2 (ended July 31): comps +0.2%, transactions -2.1%, ticket +2.3%, operating margin 13.67% against 14.48%. It recognised only about $80M of tariff refunds against Home Depot's $685M. I found no Lowe's Q3 date or preview.
Leadership: no new announcement found since the Aug 12 medical-leave headline. No successor search or return date is reported inside the 14-day window.
Bloomberg (Oct 20) describes Home Depot as stuck in a frozen housing market and drawn into the immigration-enforcement debate, a reputational and labor-related overhang rather than an earnings item.
Options market implies a ±7.2% move (as of Oct 30) against a ±2.1% average over the last 8 reports. No beat/miss record or revision data was available.

key_debates.question: Is $3.95 a GAAP or an adjusted target, and is it beatable?

bull.text: If consensus is adjusted (GAAP plus after-tax acquired-intangible amortization of about $0.13 per quarter), $3.95 is only about +5% against a derived Q3 FY25 adjusted base of about $3.75, in line with a mid-single-digit adjusted growth rate. The Street FY26 EPS of $15.01 is built off the adjusted $14.69 base.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Nov 17 release's GAAP and adjusted EPS against $3.95, the gross margin ex-refund and any management comment on refund timing.

key_debates.question: Is $44.04B of revenue (+6.5%) achievable once GMS is partly lapped?

bull.text: Acquisitions still add: Mingledorff's is a new full-quarter contributor, GMS was only partly in the Q3 FY25 base, and Other sales grew 62% in Q2. Primary comps of +1.7% plus FX tailwinds help.

bear.text: GMS contributed about $2.0B in the roughly 21 weeks after Sept 4, 2025, so Q3 FY25 already held about 8 weeks of it. My build gives Q3 of about $42.7B to $43.2B. Even at the top of the guided sales range, consensus Q3 implies Q4 growth of only about +0.6%, so either the guide is conservative or Q3 consensus is too high.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Reported Q3 net sales and the Other segment sales (versus $5,055M in Q2), plus any raise to the FY26 sales guide.

key_debates.question: Do Q3 comps stay above or fall below Q2's +1.7%?

bull.text: Home Depot out-comped Lowe's in Q2 (+1.7% vs +0.2%). 13 of the 16 Primary merchandising departments listed in the 10-K posted positive comps, and online sales rose 11.0%. Comparable sales reflect customer engagement with smaller repair and maintenance projects.

bear.text: Sentiment is near a record low, new-home sales fell 5.3% year on year, lumber is deflating and Lowe's transactions fell 2.1%. Home Depot's own transactions have fallen for the whole first half (-1.2%), so ticket does all the work. I lean to a Q3 comp of about 0% to +1.5%.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 comps, the transaction/ticket split and the US comp versus Q2's +1.3% (reported by press), plus commentary on Q4-to-date trends.

key_debates.question: Will cost pressure persist now that the refund has been received?

bull.text: About $45M of refund remains in inventory and will release as it sells. Management said refund timing could shift some margin between Q2 and Q3, and the GMS mix drag fades as the acquisition is lapped. Masco still expects a net tariff benefit for the year.

bear.text: Management expects fuel, energy and input costs to fully offset the refunds over the year. Q3 therefore carries the cost pressure without the refund tailwind. Supplier Masco cites mid-single-digit input inflation, and Lowe's gross margin fell 77bp in its Q2.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 gross margin and SG&A rate against Q3 FY25, and management's Q4 gross margin commentary.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Comps of about +2% or better with positive transaction growth, sales near $43.5B or higher with Other growth holding up. Gross margin holds near last year as the $45M refund tail and easing GMS drag offset fuel costs, and GAAP operating margin reaches about 13.1% or more. EPS is at or above $3.95 on either basis, guidance is held or nudged up, and the stock rallies beyond the ±7.2% implied move.

triggers: Comp of +2% or better with positive comparable transactions
Gross margin flat or up year on year despite no refund
Commentary that Q4-to-date trends are firm and Pro strength is accelerating
Management lifts or narrows the FY guide upward

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Revenue of about $43.0B (+4%) with comps of about +1% (ticket-led, transactions -1%). GAAP operating margin of about 12.5% to 13.0% and GAAP EPS of about $3.70 to $3.85, which is roughly $3.83 to $3.98 on an adjusted basis. That is a miss on a GAAP reading and in line on an adjusted reading, with the FY guide held. The revenue shortfall against $44.04B is the more visible miss.

triggers: Gross margin down year on year as the refund drops out
SG&A rate up year on year

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Comps of 0% or lower on weak housing and sentiment, with transactions down more than 1%. Gross margin falls noticeably as fuel and input costs bite and Other margin compresses. GAAP EPS is below $3.70 and sales are under $42.7B. Management trims the FY outlook toward the low end of the ranges, and the leadership uncertainty amplifies the reaction. The stock falls beyond ±7.2%, with the 52-week low of about $277 (as reported in early October) in play.

triggers: FY guide cut toward the low end or a weaker Q4 gross margin outlook
Negative news on CEO health or the interim arrangement

claim.text: Tariff-refund non-recurrence: the $685M recognised in Q2 flattered gross margin and EPS (about $0.52 per share by my arithmetic). Management expects fuel, energy and input costs to offset the refunds over the year, so Q3 faces the pressure without the benefit.

Weak core demand: housing turnover remains low, consumer sentiment is near a record low, new-home sales are falling, and Home Depot's comparable transactions are down year to date. Growth depends on ticket and smaller projects.
SG&A deleverage: Primary SG&A grew about 5.3% on about 1.5% Primary sales growth in Q2. Continued low comps would keep pressure on operating margin, which fell in H1 (13.2% against 13.7%).

Leadership uncertainty: the CFO is signing as Interim Principal Executive Officer after the CEO's medical leave announced Aug 12. No return date or succession plan was found, and the leave adds execution and guidance-process risk. The 10-K's risk factors already flagged management transitions generically.

Acquisition integration and mix: Other margin fell to about 4.9% from 6.4%, goodwill rose $563M in H1 (Mingledorff's HVAC created a fifth SRS vertical), and the acquired mix drags gross margin. Legacy SRS organic growth is not disclosed.

Leverage and returns: TTM ROIC fell to 24.8% from 27.2% with buybacks paused. About $9B of debt is carried in current debt and commercial paper ($4.2B commercial paper plus $4.7B current installments), and senior notes' fair value ($39.9B) is below carrying amount ($44.9B). The share count is not shrinking.

Labor and immigration-enforcement exposure: Bloomberg (Oct 20) highlights Home Depot's complicated position on immigration enforcement. The 10-K already lists immigration regulation among the factors that could raise its costs.

questions_for_management.question: What was Q3 gross margin excluding any refund-related items, and how much of the $45M of refund held in inventory flowed through Q3 against Q4? Is any further IEEPA refund expected?

why.text: About $730M of refunds have been received, $685M recognised in Q2 COGS, and the rest sits in inventory cost. Management has said timing could shift margin between quarters.

questions_for_management.question: Is the $3.95 Street EPS being compared with the right basis? How should we bridge GAAP to adjusted EPS (intangible amortization of about $180M per quarter)?

why.text: The consensus basis is unconfirmed, and the amortization add-back is worth about $0.13 per share per quarter, which changes the implied growth from +9% to about +5%.

questions_for_management.question: What is organic growth in SRS/Other by vertical (roofing, pool, landscape, interior, HVAC), what are Mingledorff's quarterly sales, and what is the GMS year-over-year contribution in Q3?

why.text: Other sales rose 62% in Q2 ($5,055M vs $3,120M), but GMS ($1.4B of incremental sales) and Mingledorff's ('immaterial') are hard to separate from legacy SRS organic growth.

questions_for_management.question: What are Q3-to-date and Q4-to-date comp trends, split between Pro and DIY and between transactions and ticket? How does the flat-to-2% comp guide map to H2?

why.text: Q2 comps were +1.7% with transactions -1.0%, H1 was +1.2%, and the full-year comp guide of flat to +2% implies a wide H2 range.

questions_for_management.question: Why did Primary SG&A grow about 5.3% on 1.5% sales growth, how much is wages, fuel and technology, and what is the plan to restore leverage?

why.text: Primary SG&A deleverage and the fall in H1 operating margin are the core margin issue once the refund is removed.

questions_for_management.question: What is the timeline for Ted Decker's return, who is making guidance decisions in the interim, and is any succession or governance change planned?

why.text: The CFO signs the 10-Q as Interim Principal Executive Officer, and a medical-leave headline dated Aug 12 is the only public explanation found.

questions_for_management.question: What leverage level triggers the resumption of buybacks, and when do you expect it? How do you weigh further acquisitions against debt paydown?

why.text: Buybacks are paused with none planned in FY26, ROIC fell to 24.8% and H1 acquisitions cost $1.3B.
